title: 领导力 Day 74：职场常用的判断框架
title_en: Leadership Day 74: Decision Frameworks for Everyday Work

questions.question: 一项季度权限审计，做得再出色回报也有限，但一旦出问题代价很大。按回报—代价矩阵，这类事该怎么处理？
options: 两头都不确定就先砍掉，等出了问题再说
代价大就要做到出色，投入团队最强的人
刚好达标但要稳：定 owner、自动化、设预警
回报有限就应付一下，把全部精力留给那些回报高的事
questions.explanation: 回报低、做砸代价高的事落在「刚好达标，但必须稳」那一格。「应付一下」是常见错误：把「够用」当成「不管」，平时没事、一出问题就是大事；而要做到出色的是回报高的事，比如答应客户的性能优化。
questions.question_en: A quarterly access audit offers little upside even if done brilliantly, but going wrong would be very costly. Under the payoff–cost matrix, how should it be handled?
options_en: Since both are uncertain, cut it and deal with problems if they arise
Since the cost of failure is high, make it excellent and assign the strongest people
Aim for just meeting the bar, but reliably: assign an owner, automate what you can, set alerts before deadlines
Since the payoff is low, do the bare minimum and save all effort for high-payoff work
questions.explanation_en: Low payoff plus high failure cost belongs in the 'good enough, but solid' box. Doing the bare minimum is the classic mistake of treating 'good enough' as 'ignore it' — fine until the one time it's a disaster; excellence is reserved for high-payoff work like the performance fix promised to a customer.

questions.question: 一个团队花两周争内部看板用哪个图表库，同一周却在十分钟的会上定下对外 API 的字段命名、第二天发给了三个合作方。问题出在哪？
options: 两件事都该快速决定，开会讨论本身就是浪费
问题在于两件事都没有指定唯一的负责人，跟决定的快慢其实无关
门弄反了：图表库可撤回该快定，对外 API 难改该慢定
两件事都该慢下来，任何技术决定都要充分评审
questions.explanation: 先问决定做错了能不能撤回：图表库随时可换，是双向门；对外 API 有人接入后很难改，是单向门。组织的慢常来自拿单向门的流程对待双向门，而真正的单向门反而被随手定了。
questions.question_en: A team spends two weeks arguing over which charting library to use for an internal dashboard, yet in the same week settles an external API's field names in a ten-minute meeting and ships them to three partners the next day. What went wrong?
options_en: Both should have been decided fast; meetings themselves are the waste
The problem was the lack of a designated owner, not the speed of decisions
The door types were swapped: the library is reversible and should be decided fast; the API is hard to change once adopted and deserved a slow premortem
Both should have been slowed down; every technical decision needs a full review
questions.explanation_en: First ask whether a wrong decision can be undone: the charting library can be swapped anytime (a two-way door), while an external API is hard to change once partners integrate (a one-way door). Organizations often slow down by treating two-way doors with one-way-door process — and then rush the real one-way doors.

questions.question: 发布前两周，工程师坚持先重写一个老模块，PM 坚持绝不延期，两人僵持不下。按「先问为什么要，再谈要什么」，第一步该做什么？
options: 把双方立场翻译成背后的利益，再找两头都满足的做法
先按期发布，重写的事以后再说，免得双方冲突进一步升级
让职级更高的人直接拍板，尽快结束争论
各让一步，把发布推迟一周、重写一半
questions.explanation: 立场是「我要什么」，利益是「我为什么要」。工程师要的是不再每周被故障叫醒，PM 要的是守住对大客户的承诺；于是按期发布、把故障最多的接口放到开关后面、下个迭代重写，两边都满足。机械折中或搁置只是在立场上比耐力。
questions.question_en: Two weeks before a release, an engineer insists on first rewriting an old module, while the PM insists there will be no delay. Following 'interests before positions', what is the first step?
options_en: Translate each side's position into the interests behind it, then look for an option that serves both
Ship on time and defer the rewrite indefinitely to keep the conflict from escalating
Have someone more senior make the call to end the argument quickly
Split the difference: delay a week and rewrite half the module
questions.explanation_en: A position is what you want; an interest is why you want it. The engineer wants to stop being paged every week; the PM wants to keep a promise to a key customer. So ship on time, put the most failure-prone endpoints behind flags, and rewrite them next iteration. Splitting the difference or shelving it is just a contest of positions.
